title: SQL injection
summary: Untrusted input can alter a database query when the application builds SQL text unsafely. Look for: general web input.
steps: Replay an observed input with a stable baseline and one harmless syntax change.
Compare true and false conditions or repeated timing controls without reading unrelated data.
Confirm that the input changes database query behavior, then preserve the exact request and response evidence.
pass_signals: Repeatable query-specific response or timing differential against controls.
kill_signals: Only generic errors, WAF blocks, or unstable timing remain.

title: Authentication
summary: A flaw in login, recovery, MFA, or session transitions can let a caller act as another user. Look for: login, session, password, mfa.
steps: Map login, recovery, MFA, and logout transitions using supplied test identities.
Compare unauthenticated, invalid-session, and valid-session behavior at each transition.
For a suspected bypass, repeat from a clean session and verify the resulting identity or protected action.
pass_signals: A lower-trust session reaches a protected identity or action reproducibly.
kill_signals: The server rejects the transition consistently or impact cannot be shown.

title: Path traversal
summary: A file path escapes its intended directory when untrusted path segments are not constrained. Look for: file, path, download, template.
steps: Locate an observed file or path parameter and establish the normal file response.
Change only that parameter to a test-owned canary path and compare with an invalid-path control.
Confirm a response from outside the intended directory without reading unrelated files.
pass_signals: A test-owned out-of-directory file is returned.
kill_signals: Only error text or an in-directory file is returned.

title: OS command injection
summary: Input reaches an operating-system command interpreter as syntax instead of data. Look for: command, ping, lookup, host.
steps: Identify an input plausibly passed to a server command and capture its normal result.
Use a benign output marker or bounded timing change with an inert control.
Repeat the effect and distinguish shell execution from validation or network latency.
pass_signals: Unique marker or repeatable command-specific timing appears.
kill_signals: A status change or generic timeout is the only signal.

title: Business logic
summary: Valid operations combine in an unintended sequence that violates a business rule. Look for: checkout, order, payment, coupon, workflow.
steps: Write down the intended workflow and state invariants for a test-owned object.
Vary one allowed step, value, or sequence at a time using reversible test data.
Re-read independent state to prove an invariant was broken, then restore it.
pass_signals: The server accepts a state transition or value forbidden by the intended workflow.
kill_signals: Only client-side display changes or expected business rules are observed.

title: Information disclosure
summary: A response or public artifact exposes information to an identity that should not receive it. Look for: general web input.
steps: Review observed responses, public files, errors, JavaScript, and metadata for unintended sensitive content.
Verify the same content is reachable without a privileged session and is not deliberately public.
Record only a redacted sample and the exact exposure path.
pass_signals: A sensitive value or internal detail is exposed to an unauthorized identity.
kill_signals: The content is public by design or contains no sensitive information.

title: Access control
summary: A server operation trusts a caller for an object or function it should reject. Look for: id, tenant, admin, role.
steps: Use supplied identities and test-owned objects to establish who should access each resource.
Replay the same request across anonymous, peer, role, and tenant contexts where available.
Compare response fields or independently observed state, not status codes alone.
pass_signals: A lower-privilege identity sees or changes another identity's protected data.
kill_signals: Every comparison is authorized or lacks a valid peer control.

title: File upload
summary: An uploaded file crosses a storage, execution, content-type, or ownership boundary. Look for: upload, attachment, multipart, import.
steps: Upload a harmless test-owned file through the observed workflow and locate its retrieval URL.
Vary one filename, type, or storage property at a time within approved reversible writes.
Confirm unsafe interpretation or unauthorized access, then delete the test file and verify cleanup.
pass_signals: The uploaded canary is executed, served with an unsafe active type, or crosses access boundaries.
kill_signals: Only safe storage and authorized retrieval occur; cleanup fails or is unavailable.

title: Race conditions
summary: Concurrent requests can pass a check before either request commits the state change. Look for: redeem, transfer, checkout, inventory.
steps: Select a reversible test-owned transaction with a clear one-time invariant.
Compare sequential requests with a small, approved concurrent pair.
Read final state independently and reconcile every side effect before reporting.
pass_signals: Concurrent requests violate an invariant that sequential controls preserve.
kill_signals: No stable differential or reliable reset exists.

title: Server-side request forgery
summary: The server fetches an attacker-chosen destination across a network trust boundary. Look for: url, webhook, fetch, preview, proxy.
steps: Identify an observed URL-fetch feature and send a unique test-owned callback URL.
Correlate the callback to the request and distinguish server fetches from browser fetches.
Use only approved, bounded destinations for any follow-up access-control proof.
pass_signals: The server makes a correlated fetch to the test-owned callback or returns an approved internal canary.
kill_signals: No correlated server-side interaction appears after the callback window.

title: XML external entity injection
summary: An XML parser resolves attacker-controlled entities beyond the intended document. Look for: xml, soap, svg.
steps: Confirm the endpoint actually parses an observed XML body.
Compare a harmless local entity or approved callback marker with an inert XML control.
Prove parser expansion or correlated callback without retrieving sensitive files.
pass_signals: The server expands the controlled entity or makes the uniquely correlated callback.
kill_signals: The body is not parsed as XML or the effect cannot be separated from normal behavior.

title: NoSQL injection
summary: A structured input changes NoSQL query operators or types rather than remaining a value. Look for: json, filter, search, mongo.
steps: Find an observed structured filter or search input and capture normal behavior.
Change only its type or operator shape using a bounded false/true pair.
Verify backend query semantics changed while avoiding broad data retrieval.
pass_signals: A repeatable operator-specific result differs from inert controls.
kill_signals: Only schema rejection or a generic error appears.

title: API testing
summary: API operations may expose objects, fields, or actions beyond the caller's role. Look for: api, openapi, swagger.
steps: Inventory documented and observed API operations, identities, and object IDs.
Compare method, object, and role behavior on test-owned records; include undocumented fields only when reversible.
Confirm any bypass through independent response or state evidence.
pass_signals: An API operation violates its documented authorization or object boundary.
kill_signals: An endpoint is merely discoverable or introspectable without impact.

title: Web cache deception
summary: A shared cache may store a private response under a URL mistaken for a public resource. Look for: cache, cdn, account, profile.
steps: Identify an authenticated GET response and evidence of a shared cache.
Use a unique test-owned URL variation that might be cached as a static resource.
Request it from a separate unauthenticated context and compare the body and cache headers.
pass_signals: A private canary response is served from the shared cache to the wrong identity.
kill_signals: No shared cache exists or the private response remains identity-bound.

title: Cross-site scripting
summary: Untrusted content is interpreted as script in another user's browser origin. Look for: general web input.
steps: Trace an observed input through its HTML, attribute, script, or DOM output context.
Use a unique harmless browser marker matched to that context.
Confirm execution in the target origin; for stored cases, re-read with a second supplied identity and clean up.
pass_signals: A fresh browser execution marker fires in the target origin.
kill_signals: Only reflection or static markup appears without executable context.

title: Cross-site request forgery
summary: A browser can send an authenticated state-changing request from an attacker-controlled origin. Look for: post, account, settings, payment.
steps: Select an approved reversible state-changing action in a cookie-authenticated session.
Compare valid, missing-token, and cross-origin requests while preserving browser cookie behavior.
Confirm the state change from an independent read and restore it.
pass_signals: A cross-origin request changes protected state without the victim's intent.
kill_signals: The browser omits credentials or server-side origin/token checks reject the action.

title: Cross-origin resource sharing
summary: A cross-origin page can read protected responses when the server grants excessive origin access. Look for: cors, origin, api.
steps: Send one untrusted Origin to an observed endpoint returning test-owned sensitive data.
Check allow-origin, allow-credentials, Vary, and actual browser credential behavior.
Confirm a cross-origin browser can read the protected response.
pass_signals: An untrusted origin reads credentialed protected data.
kill_signals: Headers alone suggest misconfiguration but browser access to protected data fails.

title: Clickjacking
summary: An attacker-controlled page can frame a sensitive action and misdirect a user's click. Look for: login, account, settings, admin.
steps: Identify a sensitive, user-initiated action exposed in a browser page.
Frame that exact page from a controlled origin and observe actual frame and cookie behavior.
Demonstrate a harmless test-owned action can be induced, then restore state.
pass_signals: The sensitive action is operable in an attacker-controlled frame.
kill_signals: Framing is blocked or only non-sensitive content can be clicked.

title: DOM-based vulnerabilities
summary: Browser-side code carries untrusted data from a source into a security-sensitive sink. Look for: javascript, location, postmessage, hash.
steps: Trace attacker-controlled browser sources to a concrete DOM, navigation, or request sink.
Exercise one in-scope source with a harmless marker and inert control.
Confirm a security-relevant DOM or request effect in the browser.
pass_signals: Observed source-to-sink flow causes a controlled security-relevant effect.
kill_signals: Static source and sink strings have no executable path between them.

title: WebSockets
summary: A WebSocket handshake or message handler may omit origin or per-message authorization checks. Look for: websocket, wss, socket.io.
steps: Capture an observed handshake and message flow using supplied identities.
Compare Origin, session, channel subscription, and per-message authorization one variable at a time.
Prove unauthorized receipt or state change with a test-owned message.
pass_signals: An unauthorized client receives or changes a protected channel.
kill_signals: The handshake succeeds but protected messages remain authorized.

title: Insecure deserialization
summary: The server reconstructs attacker-controlled objects with unsafe type or behavior assumptions. Look for: serialized, pickle, viewstate, object.
steps: Identify a serialized value the server actually accepts and establish a normal response.
Use a benign type or integrity marker in an isolated or explicitly approved test path.
Confirm server-side object handling differs from a malformed control without executing commands.
pass_signals: A controlled object property reaches an unintended server-side behavior.
kill_signals: The value is rejected before deserialization or only a parser error occurs.

title: Web LLM attacks
summary: Lower-trust text can be mistaken for instructions and drive an agent across a tool or data boundary. Look for: chat, assistant, mcp, tool.
steps: Map trusted instructions, retrieved content, user input, and available agent tools.
Place a harmless conflicting instruction in a lower-trust, test-owned surface.
Check whether the agent crosses a tool, data, or instruction boundary using a test canary.
pass_signals: The agent performs a disallowed test-owned action or reveals a protected canary due to lower-trust content.
kill_signals: The model merely repeats the text or refuses the boundary crossing.

title: GraphQL API vulnerabilities
summary: GraphQL resolvers may apply different authorization rules to fields, objects, and mutations. Look for: graphql.
steps: Inventory observed operations, arguments, mutations, and authorization context.
Compare a test-owned object query across peer identities and one bounded alias or batching case.
Verify a protected field or mutation succeeds outside its intended role.
pass_signals: A lower-privilege identity obtains a protected field or changes protected state.
kill_signals: Introspection alone or parser behavior is the only finding.

title: Server-side template injection
summary: Untrusted text is evaluated by a server template engine rather than rendered literally. Look for: template, render, theme.
steps: Identify an observed input rendered by a server template and establish literal output.
Compare a harmless expression with an escaped or inert control.
Prove evaluation by the server without reading files or invoking commands.
pass_signals: A unique arithmetic or string expression is evaluated server-side.
kill_signals: The expression is reflected literally or evaluated only in the browser.

title: Web cache poisoning
summary: An unkeyed input can change a shared cached response served to other clients. Look for: cache, cdn, x-cache.
steps: Confirm a shared cache and establish its cache key using harmless canaries.
Vary one unkeyed input on a test-owned URL and wait for the response to be cached.
Request from a second client to verify the modified response is served across identities.
pass_signals: The shared cache serves attacker-controlled content to another client.
kill_signals: The response is uncacheable or the variant remains isolated by cache key.

title: HTTP Host header attacks
summary: A proxy or application may trust a caller-supplied host when generating security-sensitive URLs or context. Look for: host, password, absolute, proxy.
steps: Establish the normal origin and any generated absolute URL on a test-owned flow.
Change Host or forwarded-host inputs one at a time with an approved canary domain.
Confirm a security-relevant generated URL, tenant context, or cached response changes.
pass_signals: The changed host crosses a reset-link, tenant, or cache trust boundary.
kill_signals: Only harmless reflection or virtual-host rejection occurs.

title: HTTP request smuggling
summary: Front-end and back-end parsers may disagree about HTTP request boundaries. Look for: reverse proxy, transfer-encoding, http/1.1.
steps: Confirm front-end/back-end HTTP parsing conditions in an isolated benchmark or explicitly approved path.
Use a bounded harmless desync marker and compare repeated controls.
Stop on shared-user effects; do not poison other users' requests.
pass_signals: Repeatable parser desynchronization is demonstrated with a harmless controlled request.
kill_signals: Only malformed-request rejection or a single timing anomaly appears.

title: OAuth authentication
summary: OAuth flow parameters or account binding may fail to preserve the initiating user's intent. Look for: oauth, oidc, redirect_uri, pkce.
steps: Map the observed authorization flow, redirect allowlist, state, PKCE, and account-linking path.
Compare one parameter at a time using supplied test accounts and controlled redirects.
Confirm token/code acceptance or account binding in the wrong security context.
pass_signals: A controlled flow binds or authorizes the wrong account or redirect.
kill_signals: The provider rejects the altered flow or no sensitive token/action crosses the boundary.

title: JWT attacks
summary: A server may accept tampered token claims when signature or claim validation is weak. Look for: jwt, bearer, token.
steps: Identify a JWT actually used by the application and decode its non-secret header and claims.
Compare an invalid signature, changed claim, and normal token in a bounded test-owned request.
Verify whether the server accepts a forged identity or privilege change.
pass_signals: The server accepts an invalid or attacker-controlled token as a protected identity.
kill_signals: Only client-side decoding or parser errors are observed.

title: Prototype pollution
summary: A merge operation may let input modify properties inherited by unrelated objects. Look for: json, javascript, merge.
steps: Locate an observed deep merge, parser, or object assignment boundary.
Use a non-persistent canary property in a test-owned object and an inert key control.
Confirm the property reaches an unrelated object or a security-sensitive sink, then reset state.
pass_signals: A controlled property crosses object boundaries and affects behavior.
kill_signals: Only the submitted object contains the canary or no reachable sink exists.

title: Essential web testing skills
summary: Reliable tests isolate one changed variable and preserve a baseline, evidence, and cleanup record. Look for: general web input.
steps: Record scope, identities, and a baseline request before any mutation.
Change one variable at a time and compare meaningful response fields or state.
Label each applicable topic tested, inconclusive, blocked, or untested; cite evidence and clean up test data.
pass_signals: A reproducible, authorized observation supports the conclusion.
kill_signals: A guess, status code, or unexecuted checklist is the only support.
